html:
A medieval Greek epic poem about a hero of the eastern frontier between the Byzantine Empire and the Arab world. It took shape in the 12th century and is the best known work of Byzantine folk poetry.

Its hero, Basil, is called Digenes, "of two races", because his father was an Arab emir who converted and married the daughter of a Byzantine general. He is an Akritas, one of the border guards of the frontier along the Euphrates. He fights bandits and wild beasts, wins a bride, defeats an Amazon warrior woman, and builds a palace by the river, before dying young.

The poem grew out of the acritic songs, ballads about these frontier fighters from the era of the Arab Byzantine wars in the 9th and 10th centuries. Versions survive in several manuscripts. Songs of Digenes lived on among Greeks in Cyprus and Pontus into modern times. The Turkish frontier hero Battal Gazi is its counterpart from the other side.
sum: A medieval Greek epic poem about a hero of the eastern frontier between the Byzantine Empire and the Arab world. It took shape in the 12th century and is the best known work of Byzantine folk poetry.
